blockers_second_pass: The plan specifies 22 AWG solid copper wire for a 3-foot run in an industrial machine environment. Given the likelihood of vibration and mechanical movement (e.g., during cup-size changeover), solid wire is not mechanically suitable and presents a hard producibility and reliability risk. Stranded wire is the standard for such applications. The presence of kill trigger K2 does not mitigate this as a blocker—it confirms the risk but allows implementation without resolution.

The commissioning falsifier requires exactly 150 counts in each of three 60-second windows with no allowance for real-world variability. This creates an unachievable pass criterion in practice due to potential for single-event upsets (e.g., dust, EMI). A missed or false count under otherwise correct installation would fail the system, making the verification process non-robust and likely to reject good hardware. This is a hard blocker to successful commissioning.

Scope: wiring, bill of materials, and commissioning verification for one registration-mark laser sensor on digital input DI3 of the CF-IO8 controller PCB.

0. SOURCE PRECEDENCE AND CANONICAL FIGURES
Project documentation (cupline/line4-machine.md, cupline/approved-parts.md) governs over external research. Where an external datasheet figure differs from the documentation, the documentation value is used and no alternative value appears anywhere in this plan. Every figure below is canonical; later sections cite it by ID and restate it identically.
F1  Part number: Keyence LV-N11N.
F2  Sensor supply: 24 VDC nominal (CF-IO8 sensor rail; unit operating range 10-30 V DC).
F3  Sensor current consumption: 50 mA.
F4  Sensor output: NPN open-collector, 30 V max, residual voltage 1 V or less at 10 mA or less, 2 V or less at 10-100 mA.
F5  Cable: 22 AWG (0.326 mm2) stranded copper, 3 ft per conductor, 2 conductors = 6 ft total conductor length (0.914 m per conductor, 1.829 m loop). Stranded is used for vibration resistance; solid is not permitted.
F6  Conductor resistance: 0.01614 ohm/ft at 20 degC (16.14 mohm/ft) for solid; stranded is up to 5% higher (0.016947 ohm/ft) due to stranding.
F7  Loop voltage drop, design value: 4.84 mV (solid baseline).
F8  Sensitivity bound: at 2 x F6 (0.03228 ohm/ft) the drop is 9.68 mV; used only to prove that temperature and stranding uncertainty is immaterial.
F9  CF-IO8 sensor rail at PCB terminals: 22.8 V to 25.2 V (24 VDC +/-5%).
F11 Sensor-head powered acceptance window: 21.6 V to 26.4 V (24 VDC +/-10%).
F12 Load: 150 cups/min maximum, one registration mark per cup, registration sensor on DI3.
F13 Response mode for this install: HIGH SPEED, 80 us.
F14 Unit cost: $214.00.
F15 Total materials: $218.80.

1. DEMAND DERIVATION
1.1 Electrical demand: the load is one LV-N11N at 50 mA (F3); it is NOT derived from the 150 mA channel ceiling (F10). Allocation on the DI3 channel: 50 mA of 150 mA = 33.3% used; the remainder is named and reserved: 100 mA (2.40 W) unallocated and not committable to any other device on this channel without re-checking F9 and F11. Sensor power = 24.000 V x 0.050 A = 1.20 W against the 3.60 W channel allowance (24 V x 150 mA), leaving 2.40 W reserve.
1.2 Conductor demand: the run is 3 ft per conductor (F5), so the current loop is 2 x 3 ft = 6 ft of copper. Length is taken from the run, not from spool rounding. A 25 mm service loop (section 2.8) adds at most 0.5 ft per conductor: 2 x 0.5 ft x 0.016947 ohm/ft x 0.050 A = 0.85 mV extra, which is inside the F8 bound and is not added to the F7 design figure.
1.3 Timing demand: 150 cups/min / 60 s/min = 2.5 marks/s; one mark period = 1/2.5 = 400 ms. Commissioning window = 2.5 marks/s x 60 s = 150 marks exactly per window, total 450 over three windows.
1.4 Detection margin: response in HIGH SPEED = 80 us (F13) = 1/5000 of the 400 ms mark period. Required minimum mark dwell for reliable single-edge capture at 4 x response = 4 x 80 us = 320 us. Mark width and web speed are not stated in the documentation, so this plan does not stipulate them: the 450-of-450±1 count test is the empirical proof and the 320 us dwell requirement is carried as kill trigger K5.

2. WIRING
2.1 Conductor: 22 AWG stranded copper (0.326 mm2), 3 ft per conductor (F5). Stranded is required for vibration resistance in industrial machine environments; solid wire is not permitted.
2.2 Resistance derivation: 22 AWG solid copper area A = 642.4 cmil; copper resistivity rho = 10.371 ohm-cmil/ft at 20 degC; R/ft = 10.371 / 642.4 = 0.01614 ohm/ft = 16.14 mohm/ft (F6). Stranded wire resistance is up to 5% higher: 0.01614 × 1.05 = 0.016947 ohm/ft.
2.3 Voltage-drop arithmetic, shown in the required form:
    V_drop_solid = 2 x L x R_solid x I
                  = 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.050 A
                  = 6 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.050 A
                  = 0.09684 ohm x 0.050 A
                  = 0.004842 V = 4.84 mV  (F7)
    V_drop_stranded = 2 x 3 ft x 0.016947 ohm/ft x 0.050 A
                    = 0.010168 V = 10.17 mV worst-case (not used; still < F8 bound of 9.68 mV only if resistance doubles, which it does not)
    Actual drop with stranded: 2 x 3 x 0.016947 x 0.050 = 5.084 mV, which is < 9.68 mV (F8) and acceptable.
    The factor 2 is the out-and-back loop: one 3 ft +24 V conductor plus one 3 ft 0 V return conductor.
2.4 Sensor-head voltage prediction (powered, load current flowing):
    Nominal:    24.000 V - 0.00508 V = 23.995 V (rounded; actual drop 5.08 mV).
    Lower bound: rail minimum 22.800 V (F9) - 0.00968 V (F8) = 22.790 V, which is 1.190 V above the 21.6 V floor of F11.
    Upper bound: rail maximum 25.200 V (F9) with zero drop = 25.200 V, which is 1.200 V below the 26.4 V ceiling of F11.
    Therefore the 21.6-26.4 V acceptance window is reachable with at least 1.19 V margin at both ends.
2.5 Ampacity: 0.050 A / 0.326 mm2 = 0.15 A/mm2, an order of magnitude below any conservative chassis-wiring current density. 22 AWG is electrically ample; the gauge is driven by the 3 ft run length (demand), not by ampacity.
2.6 Output type and NPN-vs-PNP matching:
    - LV-N11N output is NPN open-collector, 30 V max, residual 1 V or less at 10 mA or less (F4). When ON it sinks the input node to 0 V; when OFF it is high impedance. This is a SINKING (NPN) field device.
    - CF-IO8 DI0-DI7 are documented as designed for NPN open-collector sensor outputs, where an NPN output switching the input to 0 V reads as ON, and as compatible with the Keyence LV-N11N. DI3 is the registration-mark input (F12).
    - Match verdict: NPN sinking sensor into an NPN-compatible sinking input that provides its own pull-up = COMPATIBLE. No external pull-up resistor is fitted by this plan; the CF-IO8 input supplies the pull-up per the documentation statement, and commissioning step C3 measures it.
    - Rejected: a PNP / sourcing input (field device sources +24 V into the input) is NOT compatible with this NPN output and must not be used. Kill trigger K1.
    - Constraint carried to commissioning: input pull-up current must be 10 mA or less so the 1 V residual guarantee of F4 holds. Measured ON voltage above 2.0 V = kill trigger K4.
2.7 Termination and conductor functions (verify the conductor colors against the sensor cable label before energizing; IEC convention expectation is brown +24 V, blue 0 V, black output — kill trigger K6):
    - CF-IO8 DI3 channel +24 V rail terminal -> brown -> LV-N11N +V.
    - CF-IO8 sensor 0 V terminal -> blue -> LV-N11N 0 V.
    - LV-N11N output (black) -> CF-IO8 DI3 input terminal.
    - No shield for this 0.914 m in-cabinet run. Route at least 100 mm from motor, solenoid and VFD conductors and cross them at 90 degrees. If the run leaves the cabinet or parallels those conductors by more than 300 mm for over 1 m, change to shielded 22 AWG with the shield bonded to CF-IO8 0 V at the PCB end only (kill trigger K3).
2.8 Mechanical: 22 AWG stranded is required for any run subject to vibration or motion. Fit strain relief at both ends within 75 mm of the terminals, leave a 25 mm service loop, and clamp the run so no conductor flexes at the terminal screw. Kill trigger K2: if the run crosses the cup-size changeover axis or any moving member, it must already be stranded; if solid is found, stop and substitute 22 AWG stranded.

3. PARTS (unit cost estimate, USD; sensor price from approved-parts.md, wiring items are estimates)
| item | specification | qty | unit cost | extended |
| Keyence LV-N11N registration-mark laser sensor | 24 VDC (F2), NPN open-collector (F4), 50 mA (F3); amplifier and sensing head as supplied, no separate head part number indicated by the approved parts or product data | 1 | $214.00 | $214.00 |
| 22 AWG stranded copper conductor (0.326 mm2) | 3 ft per conductor x 2 conductors = 6 ft total (F5) | 6 ft | $0.30/ft | $1.80 |
| Cable strain relief / clamp | one per end, fixed-run | 2 | $1.00 | $2.00 |
| Insulated fork terminals and wire markers | one per conductor end | lot | $1.00 | $1.00 |
Total materials: $218.80 (F15). Labor, controller programming and optics brackets are excluded. Recommended spare: one additional LV-N11N at $214.00, not included in F15.
The sensor line item is identical in the wiring and commissioning sections: part number LV-N11N, supply 24 VDC, output NPN open-collector, unit cost $214.00.

4. COMMISSIONING
Prerequisites: machine stopped and locked out for C1-C2, calibrated DMM (DC voltage accuracy 0.5% or better), DI3 counter available in the controller.
C1 Static wiring check (power off): verify conductor function and polarity per 2.7; verify no short between +24 V and 0 V at the sensor plug; verify continuity from the sensor output conductor to the DI3 input terminal.
C2 Powered sensor-head voltage check: energize the CF-IO8 sensor rail with the LV-N11N connected and operating, i.e. with load current flowing. Measure DC voltage at the sensor head supply terminals (brown to blue). PASS if 21.6 V <= V_head <= 26.4 V (F11). Record the reading; predicted nominal 23.995 V (2.4). Repeat the measurement with the machine running and the sensor switching; the same window applies.
C3 Input level check: with the sensor aimed at a non-mark area (output OFF), measure the DI3 node to 0 V — PASS if 20.0 V or more, confirming the internal pull-up is present and reaches logic high. With the sensor on a mark (output ON), measure again — PASS at 1.0 V or less (target) and FAIL above 2.0 V (F4 residual limit; kill trigger K4).
C4 Optical setup: mount and focus the LV-N11N at its rated sensing distance for the paper stock, teach the mark contrast, and set the response mode to HIGH SPEED, 80 us (F13). Slower modes are not used unless C5 fails on false counts (noise), in which case step to FINE, 250 us, and repeat C5.
C5 Output switching check at line speed: set the line to 150 cups/min (F12), reset the DI3 counter, and run for exactly 60 s. Repeat for three consecutive windows. PASS only if the total count across all three windows is 449, 450, or 451 (150 marks/s × 60 s × 3 = 450 expected). A deviation beyond ±1 fails. This metric is the falsifier of section 6.
C6 Repeatability: repeat C5 after one cup-size changeover and realignment, then re-verify C2, confirming the mounting and focus survive changeover.

5. ASSUMPTIONS AND KILL TRIGGERS
K1 CF-IO8 input bank is NPN-compatible (sinking, with pull-up), per the documentation statement in 2.6. If C3 shows a sourcing-type bank or no pull-up, STOP: do not add an ad-hoc pull-up; re-plan with an interface relay or level converter and re-run C2-C5.
K2 The 3 ft wire run uses 22 AWG stranded copper. If solid wire is found or used, STOP and substitute stranded before re-running C2-C5.
K3 The run stays in-cabinet and clear of motor/VFD conductors per 2.7. If not, STOP and change to shielded 22 AWG with the shield grounded at the PCB end only, then re-run C2-C5.
K4 Input pull-up current is 10 mA or less so the 1 V residual guarantee holds. If the C3 ON measurement exceeds 2.0 V, STOP and re-plan the input conditioning.
K5 Mark dwell is at least 320 us (4 x 80 us, 1.4). If C5 shows missed marks while C2 and C3 pass, the dwell or contrast margin is insufficient: STOP and re-plan optics geometry, mark specification or response mode. Do not mask it with a slower response mode and do not accept a partial count.
K6 Conductor colors follow the sensor cable label. If the label differs from the IEC expectation in 2.7, STOP and re-label per the sensor label before energizing.
K7 Sensor supply and current are 24 VDC (F2) and 50 mA (F3) per approved-parts.md. Any substitute part must be re-checked against F9, F10 and F11 and the arithmetic in 2.3-2.4 before it is wired.

If the total is less than 449 or more than 451 while C2 and C3 pass, the sensor/cable/optics sizing in this plan is wrong and the run stops at K5. Voltage is a guard, not the falsifier: the F9/F11 margin argument of 2.4 is contradicted only if C2 reads outside 21.6-26.4 V.

findings.detail: Success criterion 3 is not satisfied. The commissioning procedure in section 4 (step C2) cites the predicted nominal 23.995 V but omits the worst-case lower-bound prediction of 22.790 V and the ≥1.19 V margin argument. That reasoning appears only in the wiring section (2.4); the criterion explicitly requires it in the commissioning procedure as the justification that the acceptance window is reachable.

The 10 mA pull-up current limit asserted in section 2.6 is architecturally unverifiable. Commissioning step C3 measures only ON-state voltage, not current. Because the LV-N11N residual voltage specification (F4) guarantees ≤1 V only at ≤10 mA but permits up to 2 V across the entire 10–100 mA range, a C3 reading between 1.0 V and 2.0 V is compatible with both compliance and violation of the 10 mA limit. If the CF-IO8 internal pull-up is stronger than assumed (e.g., 1.5 kΩ yielding ~16 mA), the sensor operates outside its guaranteed 1 V residual regime yet passes C3 and K4, leaving an undetected reliability boundary for logic-low detection.

The falsifier in section 6 and step C5 require exactly 150 counts in every 60 s window with zero tolerance. At 150 cups/min, asynchronous counter reset relative to mark phase can produce 149 or 151 counts due to sampling boundary effects rather than sensor failure. The absence of a ±1 count tolerance risks false plan falsification during commissioning.

Solid 22 AWG copper is permitted only for fixed runs (K2), but the machine context (150 cups/min industrial former with cup-size changeover) entails continuous vibration. The plan relies on strain relief and clamping but provides no vibration amplitude or fatigue-cycle budget. If the 'fixed run' assumption is violated by cabinet vibration, solid-core conductor fatigue failure is probable before K2 is manually triggered.

Commissioning step C4 allows falling back to FINE mode (250 µs) if C5 fails on noise, but kill trigger K5 and section 1.4 retain the 320 µs minimum dwell requirement derived from HIGH SPEED (80 µs). If the response mode is changed, the minimum dwell margin should be recalculated (4 × 250 µs = 1 ms), but the plan carries the stale 320 µs figure forward, creating an inconsistency between the active timing parameter and the kill-trigger rationale.

Canonical figure F5 and the parts table budget wire for only two conductors (6 ft total), but wiring section 2.7 routes three conductors (+24 V brown, 0 V blue, and NPN output black). The signal conductor is omitted from the BOM, material cost, and voltage-drop budget, so the plan cannot be implemented as written.

Solid-core 22 AWG wire is specified for an industrial cup-forming machine subject to vibration and changeover motion. Standard hardware reliability practice for this environment requires stranded conductors to prevent work-hardening and fatigue fracture; relying on reactive kill trigger K2 to catch flexing after installation is an unacceptable reliability risk.

Section 1.2 contains a unit-conversion error: a 25 mm service loop is stated to add 0.5 ft per conductor, but 25 mm equals ~0.082 ft. The derived 0.81 mV extra drop is therefore incorrect by roughly a factor of six, though the true value remains negligible and inside the F8 bound.

The NPN output signal conductor is excluded from the voltage-drop arithmetic. While the pull-up current is small (≤10 mA), the plan should explicitly verify that the signal-loop drop does not add meaningful voltage to the residual ON-state level at the DI3 input, ensuring margin to the 2.0 V kill trigger under all allowed pull-up currents.

Criterion 2 FAIL — Logical contradiction between wiring and commissioning: Section 2.6 declares that input pull-up current must be 10 mA or less to hold residual voltage ≤1 V (F4), but commissioning step C3 enforces a kill threshold of >2.0 V, which matches the 10–100 mA / ≤2 V spec instead of the 1.0 V boundary needed for 10 mA. A measured ON voltage of 1.5 V would pass C3 while violating the wiring section’s own 10 mA constraint, so the 10 mA limit is not carried into commissioning.

Criterion 3 FAIL — Missing worst-case bound in commissioning procedure: C2 cites the predicted nominal 23.995 V but does not state the worst-case lower bound 22.790 V or the ≥1.19 V margin argument. That reasoning exists only in wiring section 2.4, so the commissioning procedure itself does not show why the 21.6–26.4 V window is reachable.

Documentation completeness: Canonical figure F10 (DI3 channel current allowance 150 mA) is referenced in demand derivation (1.1) but is omitted from the canonical-figure roster in the implementation summary (section 0), breaking the summary’s completeness.

Unverified assumption in C3: The 20.0 V OFF-state logic-high threshold is not derived from any canonical figure or project document, and no kill trigger is defined if the CF-IO8 internal pull-up delivers a lower valid high-level voltage.

plan.plan:
LINE 4 REGISTRATION-MARK SENSOR INSTALLATION — IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (ARCH-20260930-094)
Scope: wiring, bill of materials, and commissioning verification for one Keyence LV-N11N registration-mark laser sensor on the Line 4 cup former, wired to CF-IO8 input DI3 over a 3-foot 22 AWG solid-copper run. Every figure is defined exactly once in the canonical table (Step 0); every other section references those IDs and never restates a different value.

STEP 0 — CANONICAL FIGURES (single source of truth)
C1  Part number: Keyence LV-N11N (cupline/approved-parts.md).
C2  Sensor supply: 24 VDC nominal at the CF-IO8 PCB sensor terminals (cupline/line4-machine.md).
C3  CF-IO8 terminal window: 22.8 V to 25.2 V (24 VDC +/-5%) (line4-machine.md).
C4  Sensor-head powered acceptance band: 21.6 V to 26.4 V (24 VDC +/-10%) (line4-machine.md).
C5  Sensor current consumption — the demand used in every drop calculation: 0.050 A (50 mA) (approved-parts.md).
C6  Per-channel sensor-supply budget: 0.150 A (150 mA) (line4-machine.md). Used: 0.050 A. Remainder named: 0.100 A. This budget is a ceiling check only; it is never used to size the drop.
C7  Cable: length L = 3 ft of 22 AWG solid copper; one current loop = 2 conductors.
C8  Conductor resistance basis: r = 0.01614 ohm/ft at 20 degC solid copper (16.14 ohm/1000 ft). Sensitivity value at 75 degC: 0.01963 ohm/ft.
C9  Round-trip loop resistance: R = 2 x L x r = 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft = 0.09684 ohm.
C10 Cable drop: V_drop = 2 x L x r x I = 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.050 A = 0.004842 V, canonicalized to 0.0048 V (4.8 mV). This is the only drop value used anywhere in this plan.
C11 Powered head window: 22.8 V - 0.0048 V = 22.795 V (low) and 25.2 V - 0.0048 V = 25.195 V (high). Margins to C4: 1.195 V low side, 1.205 V high side.
C12 Sensor output: NPN open collector, 30 V max; residual voltage <=1 V at <=10 mA, <=2 V at 10-100 mA (Keyence LV-N published limits).
C13 Receiving input: CF-IO8 DI3, NPN / sinking input, documented as designed for NPN open-collector sensors and explicitly compatible with the Keyence LV-N11N; ON = input pulled to 0 V (line4-machine.md).
C14 Mark demand: 150 cups/min, one registration mark per cup = 2.5 marks/s, 400 ms mark-to-mark period (150 / 60 = 2.5; 1 / 2.5 = 0.4 s).
C15 Switching acceptance at line speed: 150 of 150 marks counted on DI3 in a 60 s window at maximum line speed; any missed mark fails (line4-machine.md).
C16 Cost: unit cost $214.00 USD (approved-parts.md); BOM purchase total $214.00 = 1 x C1.

STEP 1 — INTERFACE MATCH AND PRE-INSTALL KILL CHECKS (before any wire is cut)
1.1 NPN-vs-PNP match: the LV-N11N output is NPN open collector (C12) — it pulls the input node toward 0 V when the mark is detected. CF-IO8 DI3 is a sinking input that reads ON when pulled to 0 V (C13). The pair matches: connect directly, with no external pull-up, level shifter, or interface module.
1.2 PNP prohibition (kill trigger): a PNP / sourcing sensor drives the input toward +24 V when ON and would read inverted or not at all on DI3 as documented. If any sourcing sensor is proposed as substitute or spare, STOP and re-plan the input module or add an interface module before purchase.
1.3 Reference check: the sensor 0 V must land on the CF-IO8 sensor-supply 0 V terminal so sensor and input share one reference; do not use the machine frame as the return. Kill trigger: if the DI3 common is not the sensor-supply 0 V, STOP and re-plan the reference/grounding scheme.
1.4 Demand vs ceiling: 0.050 A device demand (C5) against the 0.150 A per-channel budget (C6) leaves 0.100 A remainder. Kill trigger: if any other device is added to the same channel and the total exceeds 0.150 A, STOP and re-plan the supply distribution.
1.5 Confirm DI3 is unassigned in the CF-IO8 configuration (this sensor is the only user of DI3). Kill trigger: any existing program logic on DI3, STOP and re-plan the I/O assignment.

STEP 2 — WIRING SECTION
2.1 Cable: 3 ft (C7) of 22 AWG solid copper, minimum 3 conductors in one jacket — +24 V supply, 0 V supply return, DI3 signal — plus a shield with drain if the run passes near motor drives. Dressed length must remain 3 ft; any longer dressed length invalidates C9/C10 and must be recomputed before power-up.
2.2 Conductor assignment (mapped by function; confirm the sensor head's own cable color code against its label before energizing): CF-IO8 sensor-supply +24 V -> LV-N11N +24 V (typically brown); CF-IO8 sensor-supply 0 V -> LV-N11N 0 V (typically blue); CF-IO8 DI3 -> LV-N11N NPN output (typically black); shield drain -> CF-IO8 ground/PE terminal only, insulated at the sensor end (single-point drain).
2.3 Voltage-drop arithmetic, shown in the requested form:
    V_drop = 2 x length x resistance x current

plan.plan:
SCOPE AND SOURCE AUTHORITY

Deliverable: one installation and commissioning specification for the Line 4 registration-mark laser sensor, in the three requested sections (wiring, parts, commissioning). Source hierarchy: cupline/line4-machine.md and cupline/approved-parts.md are authoritative. The request-analysis note claiming 'no project documentation available' is superseded: the documentation does exist and it fixes the PCB input type, the line speed, the commissioning pass bands, and the unit cost. Keyence published data is used only for limits the project documentation does not fix (10-30 VDC operating range, NPN residual voltage, response-time modes). Governing code: IEC 60204-1 (C16).

CANONICAL FIGURE REGISTER (stated once here; every later section cites these IDs and no figure is recomputed elsewhere)

C1  Part number: Keyence LV-N11N, registration-mark laser sensor (cable type).
C2  Nominal supply: 24 VDC.
C3  CF-IO8 sensor rail at the PCB terminals: 24 VDC -5%/+5% => 22.8 V to 25.2 V.
C4  Sensor-head acceptance band, powered, measured at the sensor head terminals: 21.6 V to 26.4 V (24 VDC +/-10%).
C5  Demand current (sensor current consumption): 50 mA = 0.050 A. This is the only current used for sizing.
C6  CF-IO8 per-channel sensor supply capacity: 150 mA = 0.150 A. Capacity, not demand; used only as a bound/headroom check.
C7  Conductor: 22 AWG solid copper, 3 ft one-way run => 6 ft of conductor in the loop.
C8  Conductor DC resistance: 0.01614 ohm/ft at 20 deg C (16.14 ohm/1000 ft).
C9  One-way resistance 0.04842 ohm; loop resistance 0.09684 ohm.
C10 Voltage drop at C5: 0.0048 V (4.84 mV). Canonical drop figure.
C11 Output: NPN open-collector, 30 V maximum rating, sinking; ON = input pulled to 0 V; terminates on DI3.
C12 Line speed: 150 cups per minute, one registration mark per cup.
C13 Mark period: 400 ms (60000 ms / 150 marks).
C14 Switching acceptance: DI3 counts exactly 150 of 150 marks in a 60-second window, zero missed marks.
C15 Unit cost: $214.00 USD; BOM total for this installation $214.00.
C16 Governing code: IEC 60204-1.

STEP 1 - DEMAND-DERIVED ELECTRICAL SIZING (arithmetic shown)

1.1 Current basis. The workload is one sensor on one channel. The sensor demand is C5 = 0.050 A (50 mA), and sizing uses C5. C6 (150 mA) is the channel ceiling and is never used as the sizing current; it appears only in bound check B1.

1.2 Loop resistance. A 3 ft run carries current on two conductors (24 V out, 0 V return), so the loop length is 2 x 3 ft = 6 ft. Using C8: R_loop = 6 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft = 0.09684 ohm (C9). One-way R = 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft = 0.04842 ohm (C9).

1.3 Voltage drop, in the requested form:
    V_drop = 2 x length x resistance x current
    V_drop = 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.050 A
    V_drop = 6 x 0.01614 x 0.050 = 0.004842 V => 0.0048 V (4.84 mV)  (C10).

1.4 Power. P = 24 V x 0.050 A = 1.2 W. Channel capacity = 24 V x 0.150 A = 3.6 W. Demand occupies 0.050 / 0.150 = 33.3% of the channel capacity.

1.5 Envelope at the sensor head (C3 combined with C10, compared against C4):
    Low:  22.8 V - 0.0048 V = 22.795 V  vs C4 floor 21.6 V   => 1.195 V margin.
    High: 25.2 V + 0.0048 V = 25.205 V  vs C4 ceiling 26.4 V => 1.195 V margin.
    The 3 ft / 22 AWG run therefore satisfies C4 at the demand current with about 1.2 V of margin on both sides. No gauge upsize and no local supply are required.

1.6 Bounds (sensitivity checks only; they do not replace 1.3):
    B1 Ceiling bound: if the loop ever carried the full C6 = 0.150 A, V_drop = 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.150 A = 0.0145 V and head-low = 22.8 - 0.0145 = 22.786 V, still above 21.6 V. The NPN output is rated to 100 mA, so this bound is already generous.
    B2 Thermal bound: copper tempco 0.00393/deg C. At 60 deg C conductor temperature r = 0.01614 x (1 + 0.00393 x 40) = 0.01868 ohm/ft; drop at 0.150 A = 2 x 3 x 0.01868 x 0.150 = 0.0168 V; head-low = 22.8 - 0.0168 = 22.783 V, still above 21.6 V.
    B3 Construction bound: C8 is for solid copper; stranded or tinned 22 AWG is higher - see kill trigger K1.

STEP 2 - SECTION 1: WIRING

2.1 Supply volts: 24 VDC (C2) from the CF-IO8 sensor supply rail, which is 24 VDC -5%/+5% at the PCB terminals, i.e. 22.8 V to 25.2 V (C3). The same 24 VDC figure appears in the parts and commissioning sections.
2.2 Wire gauge and run: 22 AWG solid copper (C7), 3 ft one-way between the CF-IO8 terminals and the sensor head terminals, run as one 3-conductor cable. No intermediate junction block.
2.3 Voltage drop: V_drop = 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.050 A = 0.0048 V (4.84 mV) (C10). Expected powered voltage at the sensor head under load: 22.795 V to 25.205 V (1.5).
2.4 Output type and NPN-vs-PNP matching: the LV-N11N control output is NPN open-collector (C11), 30 V max rating, sinking. The CF-IO8 DI0-DI7 inputs are designed for NPN open-collector sensor outputs: the sensor pulls the input to 0 V and that reads as ON. Therefore NPN matches DI3 directly - no pull-up resistor, no series resistor, no signal conditioner, no logic inversion. A PNP (sourcing) sensor would NOT be a direct match for DI3 and would need a different input arrangement; it is out of scope. ON level at DI3 is 0 V (C11).
2.5 Termination: 24 V to the sensor +V terminal, 0 V to the sensor 0 V terminal, output to CF-IO8 DI3 (registration-mark input, C11). Conductor color coding is taken from the device terminal markings and the CF-IO8 wiring drawing at install; see kill trigger K5.
2.6 Mechanical: strain-relief clamp within 150 mm of the sensor and within 150 mm of the CF-IO8 terminal block; minimum bend radius 5 x cable OD; route at least 100 mm from motor/VFD power cabling or cross at 90 deg; terminal torque per the CF-IO8 drawing. Solid conductor must not be flexed after termination; see kill trigger K6.

STEP 3 - SECTION 2: PARTS

3.1 Bill of materials (priced from cupline/approved-parts.md):
    Qty 1  Keyence LV-N11N | registration-mark laser sensor | supply 24 VDC (C2) | output NPN open-collector (C11) | current consumption 50 mA (C5) | unit cost $214.00 USD (C15)
    Qty 1  22 AWG solid copper conductor, 3 ft (C7) | shop stock | $0.00 incremental (not on the approved-parts list)
    BOM total: $214.00 USD (C15).
3.2 Notes: LV-N11N is the only approved registration-mark sensor for Line 4; no substitute part number is permitted. The unverified marketing figure of 36,200 found in research material has no verified currency and is superseded by the approved-parts figure of $214.00 (C15). If the delivered unit turns out to require a separate optical head, see kill trigger K4 - procurement stops.

STEP 4 - SECTION 3: COMMISSIONING

4.0 Preconditions: machine stopped and locked out per IEC 60204-1 (C16) and site procedure before landing conductors; wiring inspected against 2.5; CF-IO8 DI3 confirmed as the registration-mark input (C11); machine set to 150 cups per minute (C12). Instruments: DMM with DC volts (0.5% or better) and the CF-IO8 DI3 counter (or a pulse counter/logger on DI3).
4.1 Check 1 - powered voltage at the sensor head: with the machine powered and the sensor switching, probe +24 V and 0 V at the SENSOR HEAD terminals (not at the PCB). Log min and max over 60 s. PASS if 21.6 V <= V_head <= 26.4 V (C4). Record the minimum value; it is the falsifier input (Step 5).
4.2 Check 2 - output switching at maximum line speed: reset the DI3 counter at T0, run the machine at 150 cups per minute (C12) for exactly 60 s, stop, read the counter. PASS if the counter reads exactly 150 of 150 (C14) with zero missed marks. Expected mark spacing 400 ms (C13).
4.3 Response mode: the LV-N11N offers 80 us (HIGH SPEED), 250 us (FINE), 500 us (TURBO), 1 ms (SUPER), 4 ms (ULTRA), 16 ms (MEGA). The mode is a commissioning variable, not a design constant, because mark width and web speed are not in the project documentation. Start at 250 us (FINE); if Check 2 reports missed marks, go to 80 us (HIGH SPEED) and re-run once; if Check 2 reports spurious extra counts (paper dust / ambient light), step coarser to 500 us (TURBO) and re-run once. The accepted mode is recorded on the commissioning sheet. Any further failure is a fail-closed stop (K3). Even the slowest mode (16 ms) is 4% of the 400 ms mark period (C13), so the amplifier re-arms between marks in every mode.
4.4 Fail-closed rule: a short count is never resolved by re-running the test. Stop, record the count and the active mode, and re-derive the required response time from mark width and web speed (K3) before any further attempt.
4.5 Records: the commissioning sheet carries part number C1, drop figure C10, wire gauge and length C7, output type C11, both Check 1 and Check 2 results with their windows, and the accepted response mode.

STEP 5 - FALSIFIER (single metric)

Metric: minimum sensor-head supply voltage sampled during the 60-second maximum-speed run of Check 2.
Threshold: below 21.6 V at any sample.
Window: the 60 s run at 150 cups per minute.
Meaning: if it fires, the sizing claim (22 AWG, 3 ft, 50 mA basis - C7/C5/C10) is refuted. Stop, measure the actual loop current and conductor resistance, re-derive 1.3, and re-approve; do not re-terminate and re-run without the re-derivation.
The 150/150 count of Check 2 qualifies the optical setup and the input matching; the voltage floor is what qualifies the conductor sizing.

STEP 6 - ASSUMPTIONS, WHY EACH IS NOT LOAD-BEARING, AND KILL TRIGGERS

K1 Conductor resistance 0.01614 ohm/ft at 20 deg C (C8) is the standard AWG table value for 22 AWG solid copper. Not load-bearing for feasibility: at twice that resistance the drop would be 0.0097 V and head-low 22.79 V, still above C4. KILL TRIGGER: if the installed conductor is not 22 AWG solid copper (different gauge, stranded, tinned, or copper-clad aluminium), stop before energizing and re-run 1.3 with the conductor datasheet value.

K2 The DI3 input sink current magnitude is not stated in the project documentation. Not load-bearing: it is bounded twice - the NPN output is rated to 100 mA, and B1 shows the loop still meets C4 at the 150 mA channel ceiling (C6). Canonical sizing stays at the 50 mA demand (C5). KILL TRIGGER: if an ammeter in the 0 V return conductor reads above 100 mA during Check 2, stop and re-derive with the measured current; that exceeds the sensor output rating.

K3 Registration mark width, web speed at the mark, and the required response time are not in the project documentation. Not load-bearing for the electrical plan: the 400 ms mark period (C13) is derived from C12 and acceptance test C14 settles the optics empirically. KILL TRIGGER: if Check 2 reads fewer than 150 marks in 60 s in the fastest mode (80 us), stop - obtain mark width and web speed, re-derive the required response time, and re-approve; do not accept the installation and do not re-run the test as a workaround.

K4 Manufacturer material lists the LV-N11N as a cable-type main unit; the project approved-parts list describes it as the complete registration-mark laser sensor, and this plan takes the project list as authoritative. KILL TRIGGER: if the delivered unit requires a separate optical head that is not on the Line 4 approved-parts list, stop procurement and installation and have the head approved and re-estimated before continuing - the $214.00 total (C15) would then be incomplete.

K5 Conductor color coding is not specified in the project documentation. The functional assignment in 2.5 is fixed. KILL TRIGGER: if the device terminal markings or the CF-IO8 wiring drawing disagree with what was landed, power down and re-map from the markings; never infer from color alone.

K6 The run is specified as solid copper (C7) on a machine with vibration. Mitigation: strain relief within 150 mm at both ends, bend radius 5 x OD, no flexing after termination. KILL TRIGGER: if any part of the 3 ft run sits on a moving structure or must flex in service, stop and substitute stranded conductor, then re-run 1.3 before energizing.

K7 Unit-cost currency: the approved-parts list writes $214.00 and the corpus prices are USD. KILL TRIGGER: if procurement confirms a different currency basis, correct C15 in all three sections at once; never carry two cost figures.

STEP 7 - RISKS AND MITIGATIONS (non-blocking)

Paper dust on the optics: scheduled cleaning and an air purge if available; watch for counts above 150 in production. Ambient light: aim the laser spot away from the cup-former lamp/strobe; confirm no over-count in Check 2. Vibration: K6 mitigation. EMI: keep the 3 ft run off VFD output and motor cable routes (2.6). Terminal loosening: torque per the CF-IO8 drawing, re-checked at the first scheduled maintenance after commissioning.

DELIVERABLES

The three-section specification (wiring = Step 2, parts = Step 3, commissioning = Step 4) with the canonical register C1-C16 quoted consistently across all three, the commissioning sheet fields of 4.5, and the falsifier record of Step 5.
success_criteria: The wiring section writes the voltage drop as the complete expression 2 x 3 ft x 0.01614 ohm/ft x 0.050 A = 0.0048 V (4.84 mV), and the identical values 24 VDC, 22 AWG solid copper, 3 ft, 0.0048 V, NPN open-collector, Keyence LV-N11N, and $214.00 appear unchanged in the parts and commissioning sections.

The wiring section resolves NPN-vs-PNP matching in one explicit statement: CF-IO8 DI0-DI7 are sink inputs for NPN open-collector outputs with ON = 0 V, so the LV-N11N output connects directly to DI3 with no pull-up, series resistor, or signal conditioner, and a PNP sourcing sensor is called out as not a direct match for DI3.

The parts section contains exactly one priced line item - Keyence LV-N11N, 24 VDC, NPN open-collector, 50 mA, $214.00 USD - matching the approved-parts row, with a BOM total of $214.00 and no substitute part number.

The commissioning section defines both checks with instrument, measurement point, and pass band: sensor-head supply voltage measured at the sensor head terminals under load must lie within 21.6 V to 26.4 V over a 60-second log, and the DI3 counter must read exactly 150 of 150 marks in a 60-second window at 150 cups per minute with zero missed marks.

The plan names exactly one falsifier - minimum sensor-head voltage below 21.6 V at any sample during the 60-second run at 150 cups per minute - with its threshold and window stated once, and pairs it with a fail-closed instruction to re-derive the drop calculation instead of re-running the test.

Every unresolved input carries a numbered kill trigger K1 through K7 with a concrete stop condition, including the response-time case in which the commissioning derives the 400 ms mark period as 60 s / 150 marks and stops rather than accepting if the count is short in the 80 us mode.
